main:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Reads n and n integers from standard input, scans forward from the first nonzero element while maintaining a running sum and a sign flag, counts each operation that keeps the sum from being zero or corrects its sign, and prints the count." main]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize sum to 0 and ans to 0; read an integer from standard input into n using scanf with the %d format specifier, without checking the return value. If the read fails, n remains uninitialized. RESULT _input_read]
            [COMMAND For i from 0 while i < n, read an integer from standard input into array element a[i]. The array a is declared as int[100000], and no bounds check is performed. RESULT _array_filled]
            [COMMAND Scan the array from i = 0 while i < n to find the first nonzero element: if a[i] > 0, set sign to 'p' and break; if a[i] < 0, set sign to 'm' and break; if a[i] == 0, continue to the next i. If the scan completes without finding a nonzero element, i becomes n and sign is left uninitialized. RESULT _first_nonzero_found]
            [COMMAND Continue with the second loop using the current i from the previous scan, so if a first nonzero element exists it is included in this loop; execute the loop body while i < n. The loop update i++ runs after each body execution, so any assignment to i inside the body causes the next checked index to be one greater than the assigned value. RESULT _second_loop_started]
            [COMMAND Inside the second loop, add a[i] to sum. RESULT _sum_updated]
            [COMMAND Inside the second loop, after updating sum, branch on the new values: if sum == 0, take the zero-sum handling path; otherwise if sum > 0 and sign == 'p', set sign to 'm'; otherwise if sum < 0 and sign == 'm', set sign to 'p'; otherwise, execute the opposite-sign adjustment path. RESULT _sum_branch_selected]
            [COMMAND Inside the zero-sum handling path, search with j starting at i+1 while j < n: if sum == a[j], continue to the next j; else if sign == 'p', increment sum, increment ans, set i = j, and break; else if sign == 'm', decrement sum, increment ans, set i = j, and break. RESULT _zero_sum_inner_loop]
            [COMMAND After the zero-sum inner search finishes, set i = j and increment ans. If the inner search broke early, j is the found index; if it exhausted normally, j is n; if it never ran, j is i+1. RESULT _zero_sum_finished]
            [COMMAND Inside the opposite-sign adjustment path, if sign == 'p', add abs(sum)+1 to ans, add abs(sum)+1 to sum, then set sign to 'm'; if sign == 'm', add abs(sum)+1 to ans, subtract abs(sum)+1 from sum, then set sign to 'p'. RESULT _opposite_sign_adjusted]
            [COMMAND After the second loop exits, print the final value of ans to standard output followed by a newline, then return 0. RESULT _output_printed]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
